title: Internal expense claim portal
provenance: SYNTHETIC. Invented for this repository; no client content. Labels authored here from statements the SoW makes explicitly — see `why` on each. Replace with the tester's own labelled designs; this exists so the harness has something to run against.
why_this_design: A deliberately weak, deliberately non-AI design. It is the harness's N/A case:
the SoW states outright that no model or AI component is used, which makes 18 of
TRUST-7's 19 checks inapplicable and six of its seven pillars WHOLLY inapplicable.
That is the shape backend/tests/test_scoring.py pins arithmetically, and this is
the design that would expose it end to end if scoring ever counted an n/a pillar
as a zero: TRUST-7 would read ~14 instead of resting on its one applicable check.
The diagram is draw.io, so it is parsed deterministically and makes no model call.
Diagram and document agree, so a verdict cannot be blamed on reconciling them.

oe_iac.why: 'Infrastructure is created by hand in the cloud console. Nothing is defined as code.'

oe_observability.why: Logging exists (request bodies to a log group) but the SoW states there is no alerting and no dashboard. Logging without alerting is part of the check, not all of it.

oe_incident_response.why: 'no on-call runbook'. No incident process is referenced anywhere.

oe_change_mgmt.why: 'no staging environment; changes deploy straight to production, and there is no documented rollback path.'

sec_least_privilege.why: 'Receipt images are written to a bucket that is readable by the whole account.' Account-wide read on a PII-bearing store is the opposite of least privilege.

sec_encryption_at_rest.why: 'Nothing in this design states an encryption-at-rest setting', against records holding bank account numbers. Silence is not a pass.

sec_encryption_transit.why: HTTPS from the browser to the load balancer, 'plain HTTP on the internal network' from there to the API. One hop encrypted, one not.

sec_secrets_mgmt.why: 'credentials are read from a configuration file deployed with the application. There is no secrets store.'

sec_network_perimeter.why: The API sits behind a load balancer rather than being exposed directly, which is 'fronted appropriately'. But no segmentation, subnet layout or boundary is described. Reasonable reviewers split between partial and fail here.

sec_identity_auth.why: Authentication is defined (username and password) so it is not absent, but 'no SSO, no MFA, and no role model beyond employee and finance', and nothing covers system-facing access.

sec_audit_logging.why: The only logging described is request bodies to a log group — not security-relevant actions, and nothing about tamper resistance.

rel_redundancy.why: 'one instance runs continuously' and 'The database runs in a single availability zone.' Two single points of failure.

rel_dr_plan.why: 'Out of scope: Disaster recovery to a second region. No RTO or RPO has been agreed.'

rel_failure_isolation.why: 'Out of scope: Retries, timeouts, or circuit breakers between the API and its dependencies.'

rel_backup.why: 'Database backups are taken manually before each release' — a backup strategy exists — but 'No restore has been documented or attempted', and the check requires a defined restore process.

perf_right_sizing.why: 'one instance ... sized for the 400-user population' ties the choice to the workload, so it is not blind over-provisioning. But no access pattern or load profile is given to justify it.

perf_caching.why: A CDN caches the static SPA. Nothing caches repeated reads of claim data. Caching is present but not where the repeated reads are.

perf_data_store_fit.why: Relational store for relational claim records with an approval workflow; receipt images in an object store rather than in the database. Both fit their access pattern.

perf_global_delivery.why: A CDN fronts the SPA, and all 400 users are internal to one country, so there is no wider geographic distribution to account for. Defensible as not_applicable instead — this label is one of the deliberately hard ones.

cost_visibility.why: 'Costs are not currently tracked per environment or per team.'

cost_elasticity.why: 'No autoscaling is configured; one instance runs continuously.' Fixed capacity.

cost_storage_lifecycle.why: 'Out of scope: Any formal data retention or deletion schedule.' Receipts and logs accumulate indefinitely.

cost_provisioning_model.why: The workload is stated to be continuous and predictable, which is the case reserved capacity exists for, and no provisioning model is discussed at all. Fail on silence; a reviewer could argue partial because the load profile itself is stated.

sus_managed_services.why: Managed CDN, managed relational database, managed object store and managed logs — but the API runs on a self-managed instance sized for peak and never idle.

sus_data_minimization.why: No retention schedule at all, and 'Logging writes the full request body, including form fields' — the footprint grows without bound and captures more than is needed.

sus_region_awareness.why: 'The region the workload runs in is not stated anywhere in this document.' No region choice is shown, so no awareness can be.

tf_explainability.why: 'No model, AI, or machine-learning component is used anywhere in this system.' There are no AI-driven decisions to explain.

tf_fairness.why: No AI outputs exist to evaluate for variation across populations.

tf_hallucination_control.why: No LLM output exists to ground.

tf_privacy.why: The check is scoped to 'PII flowing through AI components', and there are none — the design's very real PII problems are caught by sec_encryption_at_rest and sec_least_privilege instead. A reviewer who reads the check as general PII protection would say fail, which makes this a useful disagreement to measure.

rr_ai_threat_model.why: No AI component, so no prompt injection, data poisoning or model extraction surface exists.

rr_incident_response_ai.why: No AI failures to have an incident path for. General incident response is covered by oe_incident_response, which is labelled fail.

rr_validation_before_prod.why: No models or model outputs to validate before production.

ue_cost_per_unit.why: The check asks for cost per AI call or decision. There are none. General cost visibility is cost_visibility, labelled fail.

ue_model_routing.why: No models, so nothing to route between.

ss_data_residency.why: The ONE applicable TRUST-7 check: it is not AI-specific. 'The region ... is not stated anywhere in this document, and no data residency requirement has been recorded', against records holding bank account numbers.

ss_provider_dependency.why: The check is scoped to foundation model and AI vendor dependency. There is no model.

ss_abstraction.why: No AI provider calls to abstract.

ta_human_in_loop.why: 'Every decision in the workflow is made by a person.' There is no autonomous AI decision to retain a review point over.

ta_user_training.why: The check asks about understanding an AI system's outputs. There are none.

sai_inference_efficiency.why: No inference happens, so there is no inference energy footprint.

gov_model_inventory.why: No AI models to inventory or assign an owner to.

gov_audit_trail.why: No AI decisions or outputs to reconstruct. General audit logging is sec_audit_logging, labelled fail.

gov_accountability.why: No AI outputs, so no question of who is accountable for an incorrect one.
